name: macOS Tahoe Web Shell
description: Recreate the whole MacOs tahoe interface as a web app. Every app and menu should be working

goal.answer: Build a greenfield web app that recreates the macOS Tahoe 26 desktop — Liquid Glass material system, transparent menu bar with working Apple + per-app menus, Dock, draggable/resizable windows, all five OS overlays (Spotlight, Control Center, Launchpad, Mission Control, Notification Center), and a curated ~14-app suite with representative content and fully working menus, runnable via `pnpm dev`.

criteria.answer:
Dev server boots to a Tahoe desktop: `pnpm dev` starts with no errors and http://localhost:5173 renders a full-screen desktop with wallpaper, a transparent Liquid Glass menu bar (Apple logo + active-app name + menus), and a Liquid Glass Dock holding all ~14 app icons. Verify: `pnpm build` exits 0 + manual visual check.
Window manager works: apps open in windows from Dock/Launchpad/Spotlight; windows drag by title bar, resize via edges/corners, minimize to Dock, maximize/fullscreen, and close; click-to-front updates z-order and the menu bar shows the focused app's name + menus. Verify: manual interaction test.
Menus are working across all apps: each app exposes standard menus (File/Edit/View/Window/Help) plus app-specific menus; clicking opens a Tahoe-style dropdown with correct structure and navigable submenus; the Apple menu (About, System Settings, Sleep/Restart/Shut Down, Lock Screen) opens. Verify: manual per-app check.
Spotlight works: ⌘+Space (and menu-bar magnifier) opens it; typing filters apps/files; Enter launches the selected app; quick math like '2+2' shows a result. Verify: manual test.
Control Center works: top-right toggle opens the glassy panel; Dark Mode switches the desktop/Dock theme; Brightness dims the screen; Volume slider moves/mutes; Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/Focus toggles flip. Verify: manual test, dark-mode change visually observable.
Launchpad works: opens a full-screen blurred grid of all ~14 apps; clicking an icon opens that app and exits Launchpad; search filters icons. Verify: manual test.
Mission Control works: triggering it shows all open windows as an overview with the Tahoe glass-pane descend animation; clicking a window focuses it. Verify: manual test; animation observable.
Notification Center works: opening from the right edge shows widgets (clock, weather) + a notifications list. Verify: manual test.
All ~14 apps open with representative, recognizable content + working menus: Finder (sidebar + file grid), Safari (chrome + mock start page/bookmarks), Notes (list + editor, accepts in-session text), Calculator (working computation), Terminal (echoes a small built-in command set: ls, pwd, echo, clear, help), System Settings (themed panes incl. wallpaper/accent/dark-mode that actually apply), Mail (mock inbox + message view), Calendar (month grid with sample events), Messages (mock threads), TextEdit (rich text, in-session), Music (player + mock playlist), Photos (placeholder-image grid), Maps (embedded/static map view), Clock (world clock + timer UI). Verify: open each app; manual content + menu check.
Liquid Glass fidelity & theming: backdrop-filter translucency on menu bar, Dock, menus, Control Center, sidebars; light/dark mode + accent-color tints apply app-wide; a 'Reduce Transparency' accessibility toggle flattens effects. Verify: manual visual check; toggle dark mode + reduce transparency.
Build is clean and type-safe: `pnpm build` exits 0 with no TypeScript errors and `pnpm lint` passes. Verify: `pnpm build && pnpm lint`.
README documents run steps, the included apps, shell features, and known scope limits (static data, approximate Liquid Glass, desktop-only). Verify: file exists + content check.

constraints.answer: Greenfield — no existing code to preserve; working directory is empty., Desktop browsers only (mouse + keyboard, ⌘ shortcuts); no mobile/touch or responsive design., Static/representative data; no real network calls and no persistence across refresh (in-memory/session only). Calculator, Terminal, Notes, and TextEdit remain interactive in-session to avoid a broken-feeling demo., No redistribution of copyrighted Apple assets — use CSS/SVG recreations and placeholder/licensed images; Liquid Glass is an approximation via CSS backdrop-filter, not Apple's proprietary material., Runs via `pnpm dev` on http://localhost:5173; `pnpm build` and `pnpm lint` must exit 0., Provide a Reduce Transparency accessibility toggle that flattens translucent effects.

phases.answer: Foundation & Liquid Glass Shell, OS Shell Overlays, App Suite (14 Apps), Integration & Verification

assumptions.answer: The working directory is empty, so this is greenfield and Step 4 deep exploration was skipped (no existing codebase to read). Tech stack is the safe community default for a greenfield interactive web UI: React 18 + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + Framer Motion (chosen for Liquid Glass animations, Dock magnification, and the Mission Control glass-pane descend); pnpm is the package manager (npm/yarn would be equivalent). Target is desktop Chrome/Safari; mobile/touch is out of scope. Data is static/representative with no backend and no persistence across refresh; Calculator, Terminal, Notes, and TextEdit stay interactive in-session so the demo doesn't feel broken, but nothing is saved. App icons, wallpaper, and Liquid Glass are recreated in CSS/SVG or use placeholder/licensed images — no copyrighted Apple assets are redistributed, so fidelity to Tahoe is "convincing approximation," not pixel-exact. The user's "every app and menu should be working" is reconciled with their chosen static_mock depth as: the OS shell and ALL menus are fully working (open, navigate, structure correct); app content is representative; only trivially-interactable affordances that need no backend stay wired. Theming (light/dark, accent color, Reduce Transparency) is in-memory for the session.

phases.name: Foundation & Liquid Glass Shell
phases.goal: Scaffold the project and build the Liquid Glass material system, desktop, transparent menu bar with Apple + dynamic per-app menus and focus tracking, Dock, window manager, and theming — proven end-to-end with one stub app.

steps.description: Scaffold Vite + React + TS; add Tailwind, Framer Motion, ESLint, path aliases, and folder structure. Manual: dev server boots to a blank page.

Build reusable Liquid Glass material system: a <GlassSurface> component using backdrop-filter blur/saturate + translucent layers + specular highlights; CSS theme variables; a Reduce Transparency flat variant. Manual: a glass panel renders translucent over the wallpaper.
Desktop + wallpaper + transparent menu bar: full-screen desktop, wallpaper layer, transparent top bar with Apple logo, focus-driven active-app name, and a menu data model + dropdown/submenu renderer.
Window manager: draggable/resizable/min/max/close windows, z-order focus, and focus→menu-bar app-name + menus update.
Liquid Glass Dock with Framer Motion magnification; an app registry; one stub app opens from the Dock.
Theming: light/dark + accent-color tints via CSS vars app-wide; Reduce Transparency toggle flattens effects. Manual: toggle dark mode and observe Dock/menus re-tint.

phases.summary:
Phase 1 (Foundation & Liquid Glass Shell) complete — all 6 steps done, plus all three grader recommendations from the B-grade review addressed.

Built end-to-end:
- **Scaffold** (Step 1): Vite 8 + React 19 + TS 6 + Tailwind v4 + Framer Motion 13 + oxlint; `@/` path aliases; folder structure.
- **Liquid Glass material system** (Step 2): `GlassSurface` component (backdrop-filter blur/saturate + translucent layers + specular highlights + sheen), `theme.css` with light/dark/accent CSS variables, `ThemeProvider` setting data-theme/data-accent/.reduce-transparency on <html>. Reduce Transparency flattens all glass to near-opaque.
- **Desktop + menu bar** (Step 3): full-screen wallpaper, transparent Liquid Glass menu bar (Apple logo + focused-app name + per-app menus + status glyphs + live clock), full menu data model, dropdown+submenu renderer with hover-switch + click-outside/Escape, working Apple menu (About/System Settings/Sleep/Restart/Shut Down/Lock).
- **Window manager** (Step 4): draggable title bar, traffic-light buttons, 8 resize handles, maximize/minimize/restore, z-order focus → menu bar re-titles.
- **Dock** (Step 5): Liquid Glass capsule, Framer Motion magnification, click-to-launch, running indicator dots, all 14 apps in the registry.
- **Theming** (Step 6): `ThemePanel` (dark-mode toggle, 7-accent picker, Reduce Transparency toggle) wired to the menu bar's Control Center icon.

Grader recommendations addressed (this retry):
1. **Impure setWindows updaters fixed** (windows-store.tsx): `focusWindow` and `closeWindow` now read current state from a `windowsRef` mirror and call all side effects (`os.setActiveAppId`, `setFocusedId`, `zCounter++`) OUTSIDE the `setWindows` updater. The updater is now a pure map/filter — safe under StrictMode's double-invocation.
2. **App registration moved out of useMemo** (App.tsx): extracted to module-level `src/lib/app-registration.ts` (`registerAllApps()` called on import, idempotent via a `registered` flag; Finder menus extracted to `finderMenus()`). No side-effects-in-render.
3. **Runtime test added** (vitest + Testing Library + jsdom): `src/test/focus-menu-bar.test.tsx` renders the full `<App/>`, asserts the menu bar shows "Finder" on boot (data-testid="active-app-name"), clicks the Calculator Dock icon (aria-label="Launch Calculator"), and asserts the menu bar re-titles to "Calculator" — proving the focus→menu-bar wiring at runtime, not just by compilation.

Verification (all pass):
- `pnpm build` → exit 0; tsc clean; 441 modules (348.78 kB JS / 11.44 kB CSS).
- `pnpm exec oxlint` → 0 warnings, 0 errors (30 files).
- `pnpm exec vitest run` → 1 test passed (focus→menu-bar wiring).
- `pnpm dev` → boots on http://localhost:5173 in ~140ms.

The shell is a functional macOS Tahoe foundation: desktop, transparent menu bar with working Apple + per-app menus, draggable/resizable windows, Liquid Glass Dock with magnification, and live theming — with a runtime test proving the focus→menu-bar pipeline. Phase 2 builds the 5 OS overlays; Phase 3 fills in the 14 apps' real content.

grade.rationale: All gates pass; project checks validate. Phase build+lint; manual check that all 5 overlays open/close and function.

Mission Control's glass-pane descend animation and Spotlight's safe shunting-yard math evaluator are correctly implemented. Verified by real execution: `pnpm build` clean (471 modules — agent's 462 claim is slightly stale), `pnpm lint` 0/0 on 64 files (exact match), `npx vitest run` 14/14 passing including the 5 new overlay tests that directly address the prior B-grade. charter.intent: Recreate the whole MacOs tahoe interface as a web app. Every app and menu should be working
charter.wowFactor: A Tahoe desktop that feels alive — transparent Liquid Glass everywhere, a working Dock/Spotlight/Mission Control, and 14 apps you can actually open with real, navigable menus — instantly convincing as a macOS Tahoe 26 clone in the browser.
charter.confirmedScope: In: a full ~14-app curated suite (Finder, Safari, Notes, Calculator, Terminal, System Settings, Mail, Calendar, Messages, TextEdit, Music, Photos, Maps, Clock), the complete OS shell (transparent Liquid Glass menu bar with Apple + per-app menus, Dock, draggable/resizable windows, desktop + wallpaper), and all five shell overlays (Spotlight, Control Center, Launchpad, Mission Control, Notification Center), with light/dark + accent theming and a Reduce Transparency accessibility toggle. Out: real networked backends and cross-refresh persistence, mobile/touch and responsive design, pixel-exact Apple asset fidelity, and any app beyond the curated ~14.
charter.demoScript: 1) `pnpm dev`, open http://localhost:5173 → Tahoe desktop with transparent menu bar + Liquid Glass Dock over wallpaper. 2) Open apps from the Dock, Launchpad, or Spotlight (⌘+Space); windows drag, resize, minimize, fullscreen, and the menu bar re-titles to the focused app. 3) In Calculator compute 2+2, in Terminal run `help`/`ls`, in Notes type text. 4) Open Control Center → toggle Dark Mode; watch Dock/menus/apps re-tint; toggle Reduce Transparency to flatten glass. 5) Trigger Mission Control → glass pane descends into a window overview; pick a window. 6) `pnpm build && pnpm lint` exits clean.

grade.rationale: A comprehensive, well-architected macOS Tahoe recreation: 14 apps all wired via a single-source-of-truth DOCK_APPS registry, 5 overlays with real content, a full pointer-event window manager (drag/8-way resize/minimize/maximize/close/focus), pervasive Liquid Glass backdrop-filter (verified across 12+ files), and 27 genuine runtime tests (verified by reading — not proxy/sentinel). Build/lint/test all exit clean. Two minor gaps prevent an A: only 1/14 apps (Finder) has app-specific menus while the success criteria states 'each app exposes standard menus plus app-specific menus' (app-registration.ts:19-26 gives 13 apps only buildDefaultAppMenus), and the README still says '18 runtime tests' in two locations (lines 17, 73) despite the Testing section correctly saying 27 — the final-gate recomm
recommendations: App-specific menus: app-registration.ts registers only Finder with finderMenus(); the other 13 apps receive generic buildDefaultAppMenus() with no app-specific items (e.g., Safari lacks History/Bookmarks, Terminal lacks Shell, Notes lacks Format). This matters because the success criteria explicitly requires 'each app exposes standard menus plus app-specific menus' and the charter intent says 'every app and menu should be working.' Add app-specific menus to each app's registration (a History/Bookmarks menu for Safari, a Shell menu for Terminal, etc.). Proof: a test asserting each app's registe
